question: What current Georgia business-opportunity coverage, disclosure, money-handling and filing duties can affect a proposed brand offer?
conclusion: The state-hosted official 2024 Code, 2025 supplement and actual signed 2026 Act 723 reconcile the selected sections 10-1-410–417. Coverage has three promise branches and a marketing-programme-only registered-mark exception. State disclosure is 48 hours; escrow, conditional assurance and the $10 process-agent filing are distinct. The 2006 agency page remains historical evidence.

guidePatch.title: Georgia business opportunities: disclosure, payments and the state filing
guidePatch.seoTitle: Georgia business-opportunity disclosure and payment rules
guidePatch.description: Check the actual coverage branch, the 48-hour disclosure, escrow and conditional bond duties, and the service-of-process filing before a covered sale.
guidePatch.learningSummary: A registered mark does not automatically remove every Georgia business-opportunity duty. Identify the exact promise and payment, then apply the state disclosure and money-handling rules separately from federal disclosure.

sections.heading: A programme and a registered mark are only part of the test
paragraphs: For an offer enabling the purchaser to start a business, section 10-1-410 covers specified device-location promises, buying back the purchaser’s output, or a sales/marketing programme tied to a total initial payment exceeding $500. The location branch concerns the listed vending, display and amusement devices; it is not every kind of help finding customers.

The registered trademark or service-mark exception belongs to the sales/marketing-programme branch. It is not a blanket exception to the other branches. The Act also has specific business and seller exclusions. Calculate the defined initial payment, including the specified first-six-month commitments and total instalment price, before using the $500 comparison.

A seller soliciting or offering in Georgia can fall within the definition, as can a seller with its principal business place there even when soliciting nonresidents. Federal franchise and business-opportunity definitions remain separate.

sections.heading: Give the state disclosure before the first commitment
paragraphs: For a covered business-opportunity sale, give the prescribed written disclosure at least 48 hours before the earlier contract signature or receipt of consideration—money or other value. It needs Georgia’s specified cover and contents, including the actual services and training, a financial statement no older than 13 months updated for material changes, and required earnings information where claims are made.

A Part 436 federal document can replace only the state paragraphs specifically listed in section 10-1-411(c). The separate Georgia cover and the remaining state content still matter. Update the required information for material changes and at least annually. An independently applicable federal disclosure clock is not shortened by the state’s 48 hours.

sections.heading: Do not collect the whole price upfront
paragraphs: In a business-opportunity sale, the seller may collect no more than 15% of the total purchase price. Put the balance in the independent escrow account agreed by both parties. Escrow holds the money separately; release is 60 days after the purchaser starts operating or on complete contractual performance, whichever happens first.

Separately, a promise to refund the price or repurchase supplied items if the purchaser is dissatisfied, under an agreement requiring total initial payment exceeding $500, triggers the stated bond or trust of at least $75,000. The bond must come from an authorised surety; the trust must use a licensed and insured bank or savings institution in Georgia. That subsection excludes deposits from the price paid. Multilevel distribution companies have separate bond and below-$500 exception rules.

sections.heading: The service-of-process filing is not state approval
paragraphs: Section 10-1-416 requires the covered seller with Georgia purchasers/participants, agreements made there or its principal business place there to appoint the Secretary of State to receive legal process and pay the $10 filing fee. This is not approval of the offer or a substitute for ordinary entity filings.

Support income or earnings claims with documented data and supply it to the Attorney General on request. Do not advertise state endorsement or even refer to compliance with this part in the prohibited manner. Written contracts must describe the actual services, payment terms, business address and approximate delivery date.

sections.heading: Keep the seller’s brand authority separate
paragraphs: The Secretary of State distinguishes a business/trade name (often called a DBA) from a trademark or service mark identifying goods or services. Identify which entity owns the actual mark and what permission the U.S. seller has to use and sublicense it.

For example, a Singapore parent’s company name, its U.S. seller’s trading name and the mark on training material can be different records. None substitutes for the licence allowing the actual seller to grant the proposed rights.

The current application instructions say the office does not search federal or other-state registrations and cannot guarantee availability. State acceptance is not a completed assessment of competing U.S. rights.

sections.heading: A refund remedy has its own notice and return conditions
paragraphs: Section 10-1-417 provides specified violation-based remedies, including written notice to the seller within one year of the contract for its voiding/refund route. The purchaser must make the goods available for return and cannot be unjustly enriched. A late-delivery complaint or other dispute needs the actual statutory trigger; a refund is not automatic merely because the business disappoints.
The separate multilevel-contract cancellation provisions are not a general cancellation right for every franchise.

guidePatch.practicalOutput: Before taking a covered purchaser’s commitment or money, establish the coverage branch and arrange the actual disclosure, escrow, any required bond and service-of-process filing.
limitations: Selected ordinary business-opportunity duties, not every multilevel plan, industry-specific relationship law or exemption application. The actual parties, promises, mark, payments and state connections control; federal duties and U.S. brand availability remain separate.

guidePatch.title: Tennessee franchise and excise tax: who files and when
guidePatch.seoTitle: Tennessee franchise and excise tax: entities, rates and deadlines
guidePatch.description: Use Revenue’s June 2026 manual to separate the actual taxpayer, royalties and state connections, tax rates and filing clocks from franchise-sales permission.
guidePatch.learningSummary: Tennessee can tax a company that licenses rights into the state even without a local office. Identify the actual taxpayer and U.S.-connected income before applying the filing calendar; a tax account does not authorise franchise sales.

sections.heading: Start with the company that owes the tax
paragraphs: Tennessee’s franchise tax is a tax on doing business, not permission to sell a branded business. Revenue’s June 2026 manual says corporations, LLCs and other limited-liability entities can owe franchise and excise taxes. Sole proprietors and general partnerships are generally outside these taxes; specified exemptions have their own conditions.

An LLC ignored as a separate taxpayer for federal income tax is not automatically ignored by Tennessee. The manual distinguishes a single-member LLC owned by a corporation: its activity is included with the corporate owner under the stated rules. Other single-member LLCs generally remain separate state taxpayers. A Singapore parent and its U.S. LLC therefore need their actual ownership and federal classification checked, rather than assuming one federal return settles both.
A taxable entity that is inactive but has not properly ended its Tennessee registration can still owe a return and the $100 minimum franchise tax.

sections.heading: Royalties can create a Tennessee tax connection
paragraphs: For an out-of-state entity, the manual requires doing business and a substantial state connection. It specifically includes licensing intangible property for use in Tennessee and earning income from that use. A company can have the necessary connection without an office there.

The bright-line tests include Tennessee receipts exceeding the lesser of $500,000 or 25% of worldwide receipts; Tennessee property exceeding the lesser of $50,000 or 25% of total property; or Tennessee compensation exceeding the lesser of $50,000 or 25% of total compensation, calculated under the stated sourcing rules. These are not the only connections that can create liability. Below-threshold customer receipts alone also do not automatically establish it.

For a company treated as a foreign corporation under the Internal Revenue Code, Revenue separately says no income effectively connected with a U.S. trade or business means no substantial Tennessee connection for these taxes. Where that U.S. business income exists, the manual limits the relevant earnings, net worth and allocation factors to the stated U.S.-connected amounts. An applicable U.S. treaty can affect whether such income exists; foreign ownership alone does not answer that question.

sections.heading: Register promptly and use the correct tax year
paragraphs: A taxpayer must register with Revenue within 15 days after becoming subject to these taxes. The manual identifies Tennessee Taxpayer Access Point (TNTAP) as an online route. The ordinary combined return is Form FAE170; financial-institution and captive-REIT groups have a different form.

The franchise rate is 0.25% of the applicable net-worth base, with a $100 annual minimum. Excise tax is 6.5% of the applicable net-earnings base. These are state-adjusted amounts, with allocation, deductions and exemptions—not automatically worldwide group assets or gross royalty receipts.

For tax years ending on or after December 31, 2024, the excise standard deduction is the lesser of $50,000 or the stated net earnings. It applies before the share of business earnings assigned to Tennessee is calculated and can offset stated directly allocated nonbusiness earnings with any unused portion. It cannot create or increase a loss or be carried forward; combined returns receive only one deduction.

For a period ending on a month’s final day, the ordinary return is due on the 15th day of the fourth month after that period. A period ending earlier in the month uses the fourth month following that month; a 52–53-week year uses the closest month end. The manual explains separate reorganisation and short-period rules.

sections.heading: An extension to file does not postpone payment
paragraphs: Estimated payments are required when combined franchise and excise liability after credits is at least $5,000 for both the prior and current tax years. Annualise a short prior period for that test. The ordinary four due dates are the 15th day of months 4, 6 and 9 of the current tax year and month 1 of the next year. The standard quarterly amount is the lesser of 25% of annualised prior-year liability or 25% of 80% of projected current-year liability; a separate annualised-income method is available.

A seven-month filing extension generally requires a timely request and payment by the original due date of the lesser of 90% of current-year liability or 100% of prior-year liability, annualising a short prior year. Zero prior-year liability requires $100. The manual separately allows an automatic extension where sufficient timely payments mean a credit or refund is expected. An extension does not extend payment time: unpaid tax can accrue interest.

sections.heading: A franchise termination statute may cover a particular industry
paragraphs: The word franchise has another meaning in sales and relationship law. In the 2022 Servpro v. Woloski appeal, the Sixth Circuit held the cited Tennessee termination provision inapplicable to a cleaning/restoration operator because that provision covered franchises required to hold the specified Tennessee liquor licence. The opinion was marked not recommended for publication; its contract and California-addendum analysis concerned the actual agreement in that case.

This supplies an actual industry-scope distinction, not a conclusion that every Tennessee brand offer is free of state duties. Current general offer/sale filings, exemptions, advertising and other industry-specific relationship provisions have not been comprehensively established here. Independently applicable federal disclosure remains separate from a tax registration.

guidePatch.practicalOutput: Identify the actual state taxpayer and its Tennessee activities or royalty income, register within the applicable 15-day period, and schedule the return and any estimated payments. Assess brand-sale duties separately.
limitations: Selected June 2026 Revenue-manual guidance, not a complete tax calculation, exemption application, later-law or industry-specific franchise-sales survey. The 2022 case establishes its stated scope and outcome, not a complete current statutory consolidation.

question: Does Part 437’s literal $500 exception automatically follow Part 436’s current $735 minimum-payment exemption?
conclusion: Actual current eCFR and official 2026 CFR retain the $500 wording in 437.8; the 2024 final rule amends only Part 436 to $735. The 2011 statement explains an intention to follow the Franchise Rule minimum-payment requirement, and the 2025 proposal would replace the fixed amount with a direct reference. No adopted replacement or controlling interpretation reconciling the literal gap was found. Publish the exact conflict and intended relationship without pretending the proposal is law.

sections.heading: What the purchaser is buying
paragraphs: The new-business question concerns the purchaser, not how long your brand has operated. The definition also requires payment and specified representations that you or a designated person will provide locations, customers or accounts, or buy back what the purchaser produces.

The customer-provision definition can reach recommended lead-generation or locator services, customer lists and some payment-collection arrangements. General business-development advice, training and advertising alone are not treated as providing customers under that definition.

sections.heading: An established buyer can still be entering a new line
paragraphs: In a fictional offer, an existing facilities operator buys a new cleaning line, required software and a promise of named accounts. Existing trading does not itself answer whether this is a new business or line for that purchaser. Nor does calling the promise marketing support explain whether the seller will teach marketing or provide customers.

sections.heading: Keep the disclosure clock separate from the threshold mismatch
paragraphs: Where Part 437 applies, give its prescribed written disclosure and applicable earnings information at least seven calendar days before the earlier of the purchaser signing any contract connected with the sale or making a payment or providing other consideration, including through a third party. Retain the specified disclosure versions, receipts, contracts and earnings support for three years.

The two current texts use different numbers. Section 437.8’s franchise exclusion has an exception literally referring to payments below $500 and cross-referring to section 436.8(a)(1); the latter now uses $735 for payments or commitments from before opening through the first six months. The 2024 final rule changed Part 436; it did not amend Part 437.

The FTC’s 2011 explanation says the franchise exclusion follows the Franchise Rule’s minimum-payment requirement. Its 2025 proposal would replace the fixed figure with a direct reference to that requirement. That is useful evidence of the intended relationship, but the proposed replacement is not the text currently published. A $600 arrangement illustrates the mismatch: it is below $735 but not below $500. This research does not establish an authoritative resolution for that gap; it does not declare the arrangement exempt from both rules.

limitations: The $500/$735 interaction remains a genuine text/interpretation conflict after current-text and amendment-history checks. A rule proposal is not an adopted amendment; actual franchise/business-opportunity elements and independent state duties remain separate.

guidePatch.title: Arkansas franchise relationships: what the 2023 amendment changes
guidePatch.seoTitle: Arkansas franchise transfers and the 2023 relationship amendment
guidePatch.description: Read the actual 2023 amendment’s coverage, 30-day transfer response and qualified family-transfer rules with their separate agreement-date limits.
guidePatch.learningSummary: The 2023 Act changes relationship protections as well as transfers, but its provisions do not all reach the same contracts. Match the particular rule to the agreement and renewal date before assuming a transfer veto or an old federal exclusion applies.

sections.heading: The enacted amendment does not give every agreement the same treatment
paragraphs: Act 847 of 2023 removes the old reference that could exclude a franchise merely because it was covered by the federal Franchise Rule. Preparing a Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) therefore does not establish exclusion from Arkansas relationship protections.

The enacted applicability wording concerns franchises entered into, renewed or transferred after March 4, 1977 whose performance contemplates or requires an Arkansas place of business. It retains stated exclusions and adds an exclusion where both the initial franchise fee does not exceed $20,000 and the initial term does not exceed one year. The specified wholesaler–beverage-supplier relationships are covered regardless of those fee or term amounts.

This article explains the actual 2023 amendment. The complete current consolidated chapter and later merits decisions have not been verified from readable current primary bodies; this is not complete current coverage or termination advice.

sections.heading: Use the date rule for the actual provision
paragraphs: The Act’s findings and applicability amendment apply retroactively to the effective date of Act 411 of 1991. Its added franchise-owner definition, transfer amendments and new venue, material-cause and survivor provisions apply only to agreements or contracts entered into or renewed on and after Act 847’s effective date. The new franchise-owner definition includes someone with a financial interest or someone who guarantees the franchise entity’s obligations.

The legislature’s 2023 session explanation identifies August 1, 2023 as the effective date for Acts without an emergency clause or a specified effective date; Act 847 has neither. The constitutional limits stated in the applicability amendment remain relevant. Approval on April 13, 2023 is not itself the starting date for every new provision.

sections.heading: A transfer request is different from a qualified family transfer
paragraphs: For transfers to which the amended section applies, the written notice identifies the proposed buyer, address, financial qualifications and the preceding five years of business experience. Within 30 days after receipt, the franchisor must approve in writing or give written notice identifying a material deficiency in character, financial ability or experience under its existing standards, consistently applied to similarly situated franchisees. No reply within the stated 30 days means approval is deemed granted.

The buyer must agree in writing to the reasonable and legal franchise requirements then in effect. A spouse, child or heir who is operationally and financially qualified follows a separate branch: franchisor approval is not required, and the franchisor and specified related parties cannot exercise a right of first refusal over that transfer.

Outside that family branch, the amendment preserves the stated contractual right to buy the franchise or substantially all its assets on precisely the terms of a genuine third-party offer. A right of first refusal means the franchisor can match the proposed deal; it is not the same as an unrestricted veto.

sections.heading: The new contract protections have their own agreement-date limit
paragraphs: The added provisions void an outside-Arkansas venue restriction for the stated claims involving a franchise operating or doing business in Arkansas; venue means where the case must be heard, which is distinct from the law governing the contract. They require the stated good faith and fair dealing, permit termination only for material cause under objective standards, and give an immediate family member or designated heir the stated good-faith opportunity to become an owner.

Those additions share the post-effective-date agreement/renewal condition above. They do not establish that every older contract automatically receives every new provision. HB 1177 of 2025 died in committee; its proposed insurance wording did not become law through that bill.

guidePatch.practicalOutput: Identify the exact amendment and agreement/renewal date; for a transfer under the amended section, distinguish the ordinary written-notice/30-day-response route from the qualified family-transfer branch.
limitations: Explains actually read 2023 amendments and their date conditions. Complete current consolidated provisions, other exclusions and later merits decisions remain unresolved; federal disclosure and transaction-specific facts are separate. The effect of a clause choosing another jurisdiction’s law is not resolved here.

guidePatch.description: Compare the qualified disclosure exemption and registration clocks with the recovered advertising filing-and-response rule. Its newer 2026 wording remains unverified.

sections.heading: Establish the particular exemption and state connections
paragraphs: The Act prohibits covered offers/sales without registration or exemption. Section 803(6) provides the stated business-opportunity/franchise route when the specified document is delivered fourteen calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or consideration (money or other value).

Section 802 has its own business-opportunity, franchise and marketing-plan definitions, including relevant account-finding/training promises. The registered-mark/net-worth exclusion has further conditions. Section 805 puts proof of exemption/exclusion/exception on its claimant.

Section 818 separately examines offer origin/receipt, acceptance, domicile (the legally relevant home connection) and operating location. An outside outlet or internet format does not establish a blanket result for discovery calls or campaigns.

sections.heading: Registration effectiveness and advertising remain distinct
paragraphs: Section 807 describes complete filing, effectiveness normally after fifteen full business days absent stated orders/proceedings, and one-year duration. An incomplete upload does not automatically become effective.

Sections 819–822 address fraud and misleading claims, including representing a filing as approval. A separate advertising-filing rule also needs attention: the actual agency compilation recovered is the version effective August 15, 2025. The newer 2026 compilation has not been read, so the following mechanism is qualified by that version limit.

sections.heading: The recovered rule requires a response before use
paragraphs: The 2025 text of rule 660:25-5-1 says sales literature and advertising must be filed with, and responded to by, the Administrator before use. It calls for the advertising package, a review fee and the seller’s attestation that the material is not materially false or misleading and matches its latest disclosure document on file. Sending material is not the same as receiving the required response.

The current legislative text authorises advertising filing under section 807(E) and lists a $50 package-review fee in section 829(A)(3), subject to the statute’s stated fee conditions. The recovered rule still cites section 807.F. These are the actual texts; this article does not silently rewrite that reference or claim the newer administrative version has been checked.

The definitions extend beyond brochures to the stated telephone, seminar, performance, reprint and electronic material. The disclosure document already filed under section 806 is exempt from this separate filing requirement. Anti-fraud content provisions still apply whether or not an advertisement must be filed; filed advertising is also subject to section 820. The rule prohibits references to the named Oklahoma securities authorities unless requested by the Administrator.

This establishes a real filing mechanism in the recovered version, not proof that every statutory exemption removes it. The current 2026 wording and the particular offer’s exemption must still be established before using a campaign timetable.

guidePatch.practicalOutput: Establish the exact offer exemption or complete registration route; for advertising, account for the recovered filing-and-response mechanism and resolve the newer version before relying on a campaign date.
limitations: Actual definitions, state connections and exemptions control. The current legislative authority and $50 package-review fee are read; the advertising mechanism is read in the 2025 compilation, and newer 2026 consolidated administrative wording remains unresolved.

sections.heading: Parent accounts are not a funding commitment
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s Franchise Bureau publishes application, costs/source-of-funds, seller, consent-to-service, guaranty and accountant-consent forms, plus escrow, surety-bond and deposit documents. If a new U.S. seller promises training funded by a Swedish parent, identify the seller’s actual obligations, when costs fall due and the parent’s actual commitment. Parent financial statements alone do not commit that money. Accountant consent must refer to the correct statements.
